latin_text: [HARVESTER: from Allen critical translation; source location: Garin edition, Commento 1.4-1.6]
english_translation: The 'son' that is Mind is therefore what the Commento 1.6 will call, using a familiar formula derived from the Timaeus 30C7 ff., 'the intelligible world' of the Ideas. Both Ficino and Pico were acutely aware that 'son' used in this sense by the ancient Platonists could not be equated with the notion of the Son of God.
exegesis: [PLACEHOLDER: Pico establishes that the angelic Mind is identical with the intelligible world of the Ideas. This is crucial: the angelic realm is not separate from the realm of Ideas, but is the realm of Ideas. Angels are intellectual beings who embody perfect intelligible forms. SYNTHESIZER to develop the implications for angelic metaphysics.]
kabbalistic_elements: The intelligible world corresponds to the supernal Sefirot and the Kabbalistic intelligible realm ('Atziluth / Emanation world).

other_texts: On Being and Unity (being and ideas)

notes: HARVESTER context: Establishes the identity of angelic Mind with the intelligible world of Ideas. Crucial for understanding Pico's angelological metaphysics as fundamentally Platonic. Source: Allen, p. 1112-1116; Garin edition, Commento 1.4-1.6. Kabbalistic density: MODERATE (supernal Sefirot/Atziluth correspondences).
